CO-SIGNER srefinal-2: ENTRY-POINT MECHANISM -- I got this wrong first and it is corrected here, because the distinction decides whether the launch block must also fix the child's import path. There are TWO different things called 'can jcc_core be imported', and they act at different times. (a) The OPERATOR entry point, which is exactly what start.ps1 launches: `F:\jev\.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m jcc_core.run` with cwd F:/jev, measured -> EXIT 1 with 'Error while finding module specification for 'jcc_core.run' (ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'jcc_core')'. `-m` resolves the package `jcc_core` BEFORE run.py executes, so run.py:30-32 never runs, and there is no F:/jev/jcc_core to resolve. This is the case that matters, and it FAILS. (b) The sys.path-augmented import, which is NOT what the operator runs: `python -c "import sys; sys.path.insert(0,'F:/jev/packages'); import jcc_core.run"` with cwd F:/jev -> EXIT 0, stdout 'import-ok', empty stderr -- and it succeeds precisely because the probe put packages/ on the path itself, after which run.py:30-32's own `sys.path.insert(0, str(PKG.parent))` makes the internal `from jcc_core.actuator import ...` resolve. My earlier wording tested (b) and generalised to (a); that was wrong. TEAM-LEAD REFUTED MY READING AND THEY ARE RIGHT: requirement that the launch block put packages/ on the child's import path STANDS. Consequence for the fix: replacing the throwing line is not sufficient -- whatever replaces it must also make `jcc_core` resolvable by the child, since start.ps1 launches `-m jcc_core.run` and nothing else. There are also no .pth files in .venv/Lib/site-packages, and .venv/pyvenv.cfg contains no package path.

(3) The git blob id, which is a SHA-1 and not a SHA-256 at all: git hash-object returns it identically whether the file on disk is the CRLF or the LF form, because .gitattributes pins '* text=auto eol=lf' and git normalises before hashing.
